newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Bryant left trail of carnage through Port Arthur.
newsitem.headline: Bryant left trail of carnage through Port Arthur.

text.p: An unassuming young man called Martin Bryant walked into a cafe at the historic Port Arthur convict site in Tasmania on April 28, pulled a rifle from his bag and created a gruesome chapter in Australian history.

Within 24 hours, 35 people were dead in the worst shooting massacre in modern Australian history, the peace and serenity of the southern island state of Tasmania was forever shattered, and a whole nation was in mourning.
Survivors of the massacre said Bryant simply finished his lunch at The Broad Arrow Cafe, reached inside his tennis bag, pulled out a semi-automatic rifle and began shooting indiscriminately.
Those who pleaded for mercy attracted Bryant's attention and his deadly wrath, survivors said.
Minutes later 20 people were dead, some where they had sat eating their lunch.
Outside the cafe, tourists continued sightseeing and picnicing on a sunny, autumn Sunday, unaware of the carnage.
Many said they thought the gunshots were part of a stunt or a convict re-enactment and some even hurried towards the cafe to see the attraction.
As Bryant left the cafe, he began shooting at cars and buses and fleeing tourists.
After killing five more people, including a tour bus driver, Bryant drove off, but stopped a short distance later.
Nanette Mikac was fleeing, carrying her three-year-old daughter Madeline in her arms, and her six-year-old daughter Alannah.
Bryant shot and killed Mikac and Madeline. Alannah ran into the bushes and crouched behind a gum tree. Bryant stalked her to her hiding place and shot her.
Within an hour the death toll was 32.

Bryant then took three people hostage and drove to a nearby guest house where he kept police at bay until Monday morning when the cottage burnt down. Bryant was arrested by police as he fled the burning Seascape Guesthouse.
The charred remains of three hostages in the rubble of stone and twisted metal brought the death toll to 35.
Bryant was taken to hospital suffering burns, but later transfered to a maximum security prison after death threats.
On September 30, Bryant pleaded not guilty to the massacre, but on Thursday he shocked Australia and changed his plea.
Bryant laughed and smirked in the Supreme Court of Tasmania as he answered "quilty" to the 35 murders, as friends and relatives of the victims wept in court.
He also admitted to 20 counts of attempted murder, three of grievous bodily harm, four of aggravated assault, eight of wounding and two of arson.
He will be sentenced on November 19.
